title: First physical model
note: Slap, bubbles, spray, droplets, slosh — all present, but the sole's slap carried nearly all the energy: a clap with a faint wet tail.

title: A splash is many small splashes
note: Bubbles now come in pockets torn from one parcel of air; thrown-up water lands as blobs and droplets. Bubbly at last, but dark.

title: Balance
note: Brighter fizz, bubbles inside turbulent pockets damped harder, slosh fading after the step instead of leaving stray grains.

title: Drops
note: Droplet ticks moved down to 0.8–6 kHz (a 1 mm drop at 2 m/s touches down over half a millisecond); the patter ends near 0.6 s.

title: Stepping out
note: The foot lifting out is quieter than the step in; leftover ripples and a faint noise floor replace digital silence; walks vary step to step.

title: No more crackle
note: The first thing a human ear caught (it hid in the spectrograms): since v3, hundreds of droplet ticks per second crackled in the tail. Mist is now silent, a slow drop lands softly (p ∝ a·v²), and ripples settle after each step.

title: Soft knocks
note: The walk still crackled: every drip, droplet and splat landed as the same crisp click. Now each knock lasts its contact time a/v (a 2 mm drip is a dull 1 ms “tup”; its bright part is the bubble it traps), and bubbles torn from a turbulent pocket start over a cycle instead of instantly.
